'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali attacks]]
***At least 51 people are killed as [[Islamic extremism|Islamist militants]] storm three villages in central [[Mali]], near the border with [[Niger]]. It is one of the deadliest recent terror attacks in the country against civilians. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-51-killed-mali-village-raids-district-official-says-2021-08-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****The [[Taliban]] captures the capitals of the [[Kunduz Province|Kunduz]], [[Takhar Province|Takhar]], and [[Sar-e Pol Province|Sar-e Pol]] [[provinces of Afghanistan|provinces]]. In [[Kunduz]], the Taliban seize key [[government of Afghanistan|government]] buildings, leaving the government forces only in control of the [[Kunduz Airport|airport]]. In Takhar, the Taliban seize [[Taloqan]], and heavy fighting was reported as the Taliban intensifies its offensive in the north. In [[Sar-e Pol, Afghanistan|Sar-e Pol]], the Taliban drive [[Afghan Armed Forces|government forces]] out of the main [[military base]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58135148 (BBC News)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**Two policemen are killed and 21 more people are wounded as a roadside bombing explode in a street in [[Quetta]], [[Pakistan]], targeting a police mobile van near a hotel. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/9/roadside-blast-kills-two-policemen-in-southwest-pakistan (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**[[Rwandan Armed Forces|Rwandan]] and [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|Mozambican forces]] retake the city of [[Mocímboa da Praia]], the last rebel stronghold in [[Cabo Delgado Province]]. [[Rwanda]] had sent 1,000 troops to help [[Mozambique]] fight the [[Islamist]] [[insurgency]] that began in 2017. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58138507 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Hajj]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
**The [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabian]] [[Government of Saudi Arabia|government]] announces that it will begin to allow foreigners who have been vaccinated against [[COVID-19]] to participate in [[Umrah]]. Saudi authorities will begin taking travel requests tomorrow. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58135756 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a new single-day record of 2.8 million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] administered as part of a six-day special vaccination campaign, in which 2.7 million people received their first dose of the [[vaccine]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/bangladesh-immunizes-28m-people-against-covid-19-in-single-day/2328218 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] closes all places of worship, all leisure facilities including gyms and sport facilities, postpone social events and bans dine in at restaurants for two weeks after the first local COVID-19 cases in 15 months were reported in the country. All educational institutions also have ordered to return to online learning. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/seasia/2021/08/08/brunei-imposes-curbs-after-first-local-covid-19-cases-in-15-months-.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record of 39,619 new cases and 542 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4,158,729 and the nationwide death toll to 94,015. [https://www.barrons.com/news/iran-records-over-500-covid-deaths-new-high-ministry-01628418007 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 360 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 10,749. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/08/08/covid-19-record-high-360-deaths-bring-total-fatalities-to-10749 (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record of 9,690 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 210,405. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/vietnam-reports-record-9690-covid-19-infections (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Queensland]]
*****[[Cairns]] and [[Yarrabah]] enter a snap three-day [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after an "unexpected" case of COVID-19 was reported in a taxi driver from [[Kanimbla, Queensland|Kanimbla]] who was infectious in [[Far North Queensland]] for 10 days. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-08-08/cairns-covid-lockdown/100359616 (ABC News Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Fiji)|Permanent Secretary of Health]] [[James Fong]] announces that the number of COVID-19 infections are continuing to increases in parts of the country, which began with the second wave in April. [[Fiji]] is now the hardest-hit [[List of countries in Oceania|country in Oceania]] and is only second in the number of infections in the region, with the most cases being reported in the U.S. state of [[Hawaii]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/448756/covid-19-situation-worsening-in-fiji (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Tunisia]]
***[[Tunisia]] launches its "open-air" COVID-19 vaccination drive for people over the age of 40 in 300 vaccination centers across the country after six million doses of the vaccine arrived from overseas. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/08/08/Tunisia-launches-vaccine-open-day-against-Delta-variant-driven-spike (Al Arabiya)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***The [[United Kingdom]] lifts its [[quarantine]] requirement for fully [[COVID-19 vaccination|vaccinated]] travellers who are returning from or intend to visit [[France]], due to changes in the 'traffic light' system for [[international travel]] that saw the suspension of plans to implement a "watchlist". [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-58130944 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Tech company [[Alibaba Group]] fires multiple senior executives who had silenced an internal complaint of rape and had ordered a social media blackout of the complaint ([[:zh:阿里巴巴员工被性侵案|Chinese: 阿里巴巴员工被性侵案]]). The case shed light on [[rape in China]] and exposed the [[business culture]] of forcing female employees to act as [[Host and hostess clubs#China|hostesses]] to entertain business clients. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/08/business/alibaba-rape-china-metoo.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Chinese prosecutors file a lawsuit against the tech conglomerate [[Tencent]], alleging that the company's "youth mode" for the [[WeChat]] application violates [[Minor_(law)|laws protecting minors]]. Authorities did not specify as to which laws the application violates. [https://www.theverge.com/2021/8/8/22615392/china-lawsuit-wechat-tencent-youth-mode-tech (''The Verge'')]
*Russian opposition activist [[Lyubov Sobol]], a prominent ally of [[Alexei Navalny]], leaves Russia, days after being sentenced to eighteen months of parole-like restrictions. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/close-ally-kremlin-critic-navalny-leaves-russia-amid-crackdown-rt-ren-tv-cite-2021-08-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Protests against the [[Military rule in Myanmar|military government]] occur across [[Myanmar]] in honor of the anniversary of the [[8888 Uprising]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/anti-military-protests-myanmar-anniversary-1988-uprising-2021-08-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 Summer Olympics]]
**The Summer Olympics officially end in [[Tokyo]] with the [[2020 Summer Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]]. The [[United States]] won [[2020 Summer Olympics medal table|the most]] [[Olympic medal|medals]] and also won the most gold medals, with 113 total medals and 39 gold medals. The [[Olympic Flag]] is handed over to the [[List of mayors of Paris|Mayor of Paris]] [[Anne Hidalgo]] in preparation for the [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Games]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/olympics/tokyo-olympics-closing-ceremony-set-bring-imperfect-irrepressible-games-end-n1276009 (NBC News)]
*[[2021 MotoGP World Championship]]
**The [[2021 Styrian motorcycle Grand Prix|Styrian Grand Prix]] is red-flagged in lap 3 after a collision involving Spanish [[Dani Pedrosa]] and Italian [[Lorenzo Savadori]] that destroyed both motorcycles. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20210808-styrian-grand-prix-halted-as-crashed-bikes-burns (Radio France Internationale)]
